newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-Danske Bank tax down, dividend up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Danske Bank tax down, dividend up.

text.p: Lower taxes and higher dividends could be elements in the upcoming 1996 full year result for Denmark's biggest bank Den Danske Bank, analysts told Reuters on Thursday.
Some analysts' estimates indicate that the bank's tax liability for 1996 could fall to 300-500 million crowns, compared to 1.5 billion crowns in 1995.
"It could well be that not much tax will have to be paid due to the considerable appreciation in the value of shares of Danica, Den Danske's wholly-owned insurance subsidiary," one analyst said.
Danish law exempts life insurance companies and investors generally from paying tax on financial gains on shareholdings after three years.

Also of market interest is the size of Den Danske's 1996 dividend, as Danish banks are attracting an increasing number of foreign investors, putting pressure on them to raise dividends, the analysts said.
"Den Danske Bank's management is in a bit of a dilemma on dividends," an analyst told Reuters.
"The bank has about five billion crowns it does not know what to do with and which is not yielding enough," he said.

"It is difficult to tell the public that you are going to sack 500 staff and then reward shareholders with a bumper dividend, however logical it might be to reduce staff and pay out better dividends with slack capital," he added.
Den Danske Bank, like other banks in Denmark, has announced major staff reduction and rationalisation schemes in recent weeks.
Analysts polled by Reuters last Monday forecast an average 4.8 billion crown 1996 pre-tax and extraordinary profit for Den Danske Bank, compared to 6.034 billion crowns in the previous year.
The panel saw the dividend rising on average to 16.6 crowns per 100 crown share from 1995's 16 crowns.
Den Danske Bank is due to announce its 1996 full year result on February 20.
